905 collected Medicaid.

41 collected unemployment.

Thankfully, the Trump Administration has stripped these dangerous illegals of taxpayer-funded benefits and revoked their parole status.

Obamacare expanded Medicaid far beyond its intended purpose.

In many cases, the federal government pays states MORE to cover ABLE-BODIED adults than the vulnerable, such as pregnant women and disabled children.

This is simply unsustainable—and it’s up to Congress to fix it.

The American people SUPPORT Medicaid reform.

Congress must seize the moment and deliver significant reform to ensure Medicaid is on a sustainable path for the vulnerable groups it’s intended to serve.

cc: House Republicans https://t.co/emmGb2uq3B

Obamacare drastically expanded Medicaid—exacerbating waste, fraud, and abuse.

Congress must fix Medicaid to ensure it can help the vulnerable Americans it was originally intended to serve.

Inaction on this matter is irresponsible and unacceptable.

It is fundamentally WRONG for the federal government to pay states MORE for able-bodied, working-age adults on Medicaid than pregnant women, children, seniors, and disabled Americans on Medicaid.

This has to be addressed in budget reconciliation.

Full stop.

Medicaid is BROKEN.

It’ll take courage, but Congress can—and must—fix it through budget reconciliation. https://t.co/bygeQ7UmQk

Republicans have a critical choice:

Will we worsen Obamacare’s expansion of Medicaid?

Or will we fix its flaws to ensure Medicaid works for the vulnerable Americans it was originally intended to serve?

Under the current budget reconciliation bill, workforce requirements for able-bodied adults on Medicaid don’t kick in until 2029.

Even then, they are subject to massive waivers.

Inexcusable is an understatement.

In an effort to advance President Trump’s agenda, I voted “Present” during tonight’s Budget Committee markup to allow the legislation to move forward as we continue to improve it.

We’ve made progress in negotiations, including moving work requirements for Medicaid forward, restricting future Green New Scam subsidies, and eliminating both the taxation and registration of suppressors under the NFA.

Yet there’s still additional important work to be done to include as many America First priorities in President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill as possible.

I’m fighting for key conservative wins—including reducing deficit spending, fixing Medicaid to prioritize vulnerable Americans, slashing more Green New Scam subsidies, and restoring additional 2A constitutional rights.

I will continue negotiating in good faith to improve this legislation before we pass the final product.

This is a rare opportunity to deliver real change for the American people. We can—and must—seize the moment.

Given the progress that we’ve made, it’s time for Republicans to be courageous.

We’ve made progress in negotiations—but the budget reconciliation bill does not yet meet the moment.

There’s simply no reason the federal government should give states 7X more funding for able-bodied adults on Medicaid than vulnerable Americans. https://t.co/vqKZN988RJ

President Trump is 100% right: We must eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse in Medicaid.

That includes moving work requirements up and leveling the playing field so the federal government isn’t paying $9 for able-bodied adults and only $1.33 for vulnerable Americans. https://t.co/xcxmGxwyl1
